text: What distinguishes ontic structural realism (Ladyman, French) from Worrall's epistemic structural realism?
choices: Ontic structural realism claims we can know only the structure of the world while remaining agnostic about the objects instantiating it.

Ontic structural realism makes the ontological claim that there are no individual objects with intrinsic natures at the fundamental level—only structure exists—whereas the epistemic version is merely a thesis about the limits of our knowledge.
Ontic structural realism restricts realism to the observable structure of phenomena, whereas the epistemic version extends it to unobservables.
Ontic structural realism abandons realism about mathematical structure, whereas the epistemic version preserves it.
explanation: Epistemic structural realism (Worrall) is an epistemic thesis: there are objects, but we know only their structural/relational properties, not their intrinsic natures. Ontic structural realism (Ladyman, French) goes further ontologically: there simply are no individuals underlying the structure—structure is all there is. Distractor 0 states the epistemic view, which is precisely the position ontic structural realism moves beyond.
